segments.t: In the lobby, the paramedic explains that severe overeating triggered the prefect's collapse. After Eleonora berates Mikhail for risking a man's life over a bet, Barinov hands Mikhail a fresh two-kilogram steak to eat himself.

Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
'Doctor, what is wrong with him?' Asking whether doctor what is wrong with him puts Barinov right on the defensive.
'The examination will show more precisely.' Since the examination will show more precisely, the doctor does not waste words on excuses.
'A common case, overeating is to blame for everything.' Mentioning that a common case overeating is to blame for everything moves the talk in a new direction.
'One must restrain oneself.' The doctor reminds Barinov that one must restrain oneself before the moment passes.

'You, by the way, should keep that in mind too.' Because Barinov by the way should keep that in mind, the doctor treats the matter as settled. Even in the middle of the drama, he keeps the polite plural "you" that workplace Russian expects.

'You drove the prefect to a heart attack!' Eleonora insists that Barinov drove the prefect to a heart attack, leaving Barinov no room to argue. Russian puts the key word right up front so her emotion lands on the first beat.
'Risking a human life for the sake of a victory!' With the bet and point at stake, Eleonora reacts without holding back.
'The wager continues.' Claiming that the wager continues sounds confident, even if the doctor has doubts.

'This is for you, Mikhail Dzhekovich.' Pointing out that this is for the doctor Mikhail Dzhekovich gives the doctor a sobering reality check. Even in the middle of the drama, he keeps the polite plural "you" that workplace Russian expects.
'Enjoy your meal.' Telling the doctor to enjoy the doctor's meal is how Barinov lays out the situation for the doctor.
'Enjoy your meal, Mikhail.' Realizing that Barinov should enjoy Barinov's meal changes how Eleonora handles the situation.

'Eat everything down to the last piece.' Eating everything down to the last piece moves the conversation forward without extra drama. Alright, let's hear the entire conversation one more time from start to finish.

Stuck with a two-kilogram steak in front of him, Mikhail gets a taste of his own medicine while the kitchen celebrates. See you next time!
